message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code (Title 2, Subtitle B). Here’s an overview of key rights you typically enjoy: | Category | Typical Tenant Rights | |----------|-----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlords may charge up to one month’s rent for residential units; two months for furnished rentals.
• Must be returned within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear and tear. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlord must keep premises safe, sanitary, and structurally sound.
• Tenants can withhold rent if major repairs aren’t made, but must follow proper notice procedures. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 14‑day written notice before eviction proceedings.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements; 60‑days for longer leases. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without reasonable notice (usually 24 hours) except emergencies. | | **Anti‑Discrimination** | • Fair Housing Act protects against discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, family status, etc. | | **Lease Terms** | • Written lease required for leases >1 year.
• Certain clauses (e.g., “no pets” or “no smoking”) must be clearly stated. | | **Rent Increases** | • No limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but must give proper notice (typically 30 days for month‑to‑month). | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in court; tenant has right to contest. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord responsible for heating, plumbing, electrical, and structural maintenance. | ### Practical Steps If You’re Facing Issues 1. **Document Everything** – Keep records of all communications, receipts, photos of damage, etc. 2. **Written Notice** – Send a certified letter or email confirming receipt of your notice. 3. **Seek Mediation** – Many counties offer free mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes. 4. **Legal Aid** – Contact local legal aid organizations or the Texas Legal Services Center for assistance. If you need a formal document—like a lease agreement or a notice of intent to terminate—you can let me know the specifics, and I can help draft it.
